name: Neuromuscular Junction Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Neuromuscular Junction Disease

criteria.description: Presence of fluctuating muscle weakness and fatigability
Electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission (e.g., decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation)
Detection of pathogenic autoantibodies against neuromuscular junction components (e.g., acetylcholine receptor antibodies)
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or immunotherapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fluctuating muscle weakness plus electrophysiological evidence of impaired neuromuscular transmission
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Autoantibody testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; response to treatment is supportive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ocular muscle fatigability leading to ptosis and diplopia
searchTerms: double vision from eye muscle fatigue

common.symptomName: Bulbar muscle weakness causing dysarthria and dysphagia
searchTerms: weak throat muscles causing speech and swallowing issues
bulbar weakness with dysarthria and dysphagia
difficulty speaking and swallowing from muscle weakness
weakness in upper arm and thigh muscles

common.symptomName: Respiratory muscle weakness with dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to weak breathing muscles

common.symptomName: Improvement of muscle strength after rest

rare.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction (e.g., dry mouth, orthostatic hypotension)
rare.notes: Note: autonomic is not a valid bodySystem per schema, replaced with neurological
searchTerms: dry mouth and dizziness when standing

laboratory: Presence of acetylcholine receptor antibodies or anti-MuSK antibodies
Elevated serum creatine kinase usually absent or mildly elevated
imaging: Chest CT or MRI to detect thymoma
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding neuromuscular junction proteins in congenital forms (e.g., CHRNE, RAPSN)
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Improvement of muscle strength with repeated use
Presence of voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies
Early onset in infancy or childhood

redFlags: Rapid progression of respiratory muscle weakness
Sudden onset of bulbar symptoms with choking or aspiration
references: Drachman DB. Myasthenia Gravis. N Engl J Med. 1994;330(25):1797-1810.
Gilhus NE. Myasthenia Gravis. N Engl J Med. 2016;375(26):2570-2581.
